deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1983–84 notes on systems of pseudolines (pseudo-line arrangements in the projective plane). 𝒳 is a combinatorial space or complex of configurations, apparently pseudoline arrangements, or positions of a moving pseudoline ("p.r.") relative to a fixed system Σ. Moves are elementary operations: passing a pseudoline over a vertex (triangle flips / mutations). 𝒳̃ is some covering, perhaps an oriented or marked version. There is a monodromy representation π_1(𝒳) → D_{2n}. Here D_{2n} is the dihedral symmetry group of the cyclically ordered 2n ends (directions at infinity) of n pseudolines, i.e. it acts on ℤ/2n.

Step 1 (the boxed formula). Parallel transport along a half-turn, starting from a pseudo-singular position, induces the shift λ(t) = t − (n−1) on ℤ/2n.
- gcd(n−1, 2n) = 1 if n is even and 2 if n is odd.
- So the image of π_1(𝒳) contains the full rotation subgroup D⁺_{2n} ≅ ℤ/2n (index ≤ 2) when n is even.
- When n is odd it contains the index-2 subgroup of rotations ≅ ℤ/n, so the image has index 1, 2 or 4.

Step 2. For the covering 𝒳̃, transport along the pseudo-singular components of K gives λ'(t) = t − 2(n−1). Since gcd(2(n−1), 2n) = 2, the image of π_1(𝒳̃) always contains ℤ/n, of index 4 in D_{2n). The quotient is D_2 ≅ 𝔽_2 × 𝔽_2 (Klein four group).

Step 3. This leaves open the image of the remaining elements π_1(𝒳) ∖ π_1(𝒳̃), in particular their image under the orientation character χ: D_{2n} → ±1 (rotations ↦ +1, reflections ↦ −1). Strategy: pivot a pseudoline by a half-turn around a vertex of Σ through elementary steps. The orientation of the pseudo-singular position is reversed, and χ(λ) is determined by the parity of the number of steps (+1 if odd, −1 if even). One therefore wants loops with an even number of steps.

The next page carries this out. The step count is 2·(number of multiple vertices met) + order of s. So the sign depends on the parity of the index ν(s), and a single simple vertex suffices for surjectivity of π_1(𝒳) → ±1 (and of the covering's π_1). Combined with Step 1, for n even this gives surjectivity of π_1(𝒳^{ess}) → D_{2n}.

Overall purpose: compute the monodromy group of the space of pseudoline configurations acting on the dihedral symmetry of the line at infinity, a kind of 'Galois/monodromy group' of the moduli of pseudoline arrangements.
errors: The text says 'le pgcd de 2(n−1) et n est 1 ou 2'. For the subgroup of ℤ/2n generated by 2(n−1), the relevant number is gcd(2(n−1), 2n) = 2, always. The stated conclusion (image contains ℤ/n, index 4) is nonetheless correct.
The parenthetical identification for n even reads '≃ ℤ/nℤ' in the transcription. D⁺_{2n} (rotations of the 2n-gon) is ℤ/2nℤ; the handwriting appears to say ℤ/2nℤ.
'Image of π_1(𝒳) − π_1(𝒳̃)' is loose: it means the coset or complement, not a group.

The sign rule χ(λ) = +1 iff the number of steps is odd depends on a normalization (the orientation reversal contributes one sign) that is not stated explicitly. The next page also corrects the counting, noting that non-pseudo-geodesic flips have order 2(n−1), not 2n.

ideas.what: Monodromy of the space of pseudoline configurations on the dihedral group D_{2n} acting on the 2n ends at infinity; parallel transport along a half-turn gives the shift t ↦ t−(n−1)
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy / rotation action on circular sequences of permutations; flip graph of pseudoline arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, ~1980–84); Ringel (1956) for flip connectivity

ideas.what: Index computation via gcd: image contains ℤ/2n (n even) or ℤ/n (n odd); for the covering always ℤ/n of index 4 with Klein-four quotient
Determining the orientation character χ: π_1 → ±1 by counting the parity of elementary moves when a pseudoline pivots a half-turn around a vertex
ideas.modern_name: Parity/sign of flip sequences (mutation parity) in pseudoline arrangements

missed.claim: A program to compute the full monodromy group π_1(𝒳) → D_{2n} of the configuration space of pseudoline systems, using parity of flip counts around a vertex. Partial results: always contains ℤ/n; surjective onto ±1 when a simple vertex exists; surjective onto D_{2n} for n even. The open question (whether π_1(𝒳̃) → D_{2n} is surjective) is left explicitly unresolved.
missed.quote: Ceci ne nous dit rien sur l'image de π_1(𝒳) − π_1(𝒳̃) dans D_{2n}, et en particulier sur son image dans ±1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Topology of flip graphs and of spaces of pseudoline arrangements, and their monodromy on the cyclic structure at infinity, is studied piecemeal (allowable sequences, Mnëv universality, oriented-matroid spaces). An explicit dihedral monodromy statement with parity criterion via vertex index does not appear to be standard.

missed.claim: Implicit link between Goodman–Pollack circular/allowable sequences (rotation by half-turn shifting labels by n−1) and a covering-space/monodromy viewpoint on the moduli of pseudoline arrangements.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This frames combinatorial sweeps as fundamental-group elements of a configuration space, a viewpoint close to later work on the topology of the space of oriented matroids/pseudoline arrangements.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful working computation, unpublished and in an area (pseudoline arrangements) Grothendieck is not known for. The individual steps are elementary group theory plus move-parity counting, and probably of limited novelty to specialists.
transcription_corrections: '(si n pair ≃ ℤ/nℤ d'indice 1 ou 2)' is likely '≃ ℤ/2nℤ' in the image.
'faire pivoter une p.r.' — p.r. is likely 'pseudo-droite' abbreviation or 'pseudo-rectiligne'; unclear.
Marginal note: something like 'Attention au pivot autour des sommets de Pol(D) ... au p.r.'; mostly illegible.
Vertical note 'Tout le reste continu!' is correctly placed as a marginal remark.
